Thanks again for the call today — good overview and appreciate the demo. A couple of quick questions from our engineering lead before we move forward with a pilot:

- SDKs & auth: do you have a recommended SDK/flow for server-side calls from our backend (node/java)? Any example for integrating with our existing KMS?
- Routing & policy: we heard about routing policies (latency vs cost). Can you summarize how we’d express a policy that prefers low-latency for chat but falls back to cheaper models for batch summaries?
- Structured output / tool calling: we want to call internal tools (ticketing, search) — how opinionated is Redwood on tool calling vs returning structured JSON?
- Embeddings/rerankers: for semantic search + reranking we currently use OpenSearch + custom reranker. Any recommended architecture to use Redwood embeddings + reranker with a fallback to our existing pipeline?

If you can send a short post-call recap with next steps and any architecture sketches that’d be great.

Best,

Elena — great speaking with you and the ACME team today. Recap + next steps below. I’ve attached a short MVP integration note and a diagram.

Recap (short):
- Goal: pilot Redwood for customer-facing chat (low-latency) + nightly batch summarization (cost-sensitive).
- Infra: ACME backend (Node.js), internal KMS for keys, OpenSearch for document store + existing reranker.

Answers & recommended approach:
1) SDKs & auth
- Use our official Node SDK for server-to-server calls (example: initialize with service token, rotate via your KMS). We support request-level API keys plus optional mTLS for private deployments.
- Example flow: ACME KMS -> Redwood Secrets Manager (or pass short-lived token) -> SDK call. See attached snippet in the Drive link.

2) Model routing & policies (high-level)
- Define routes per logical workload (chat, summarization, embeddings). Each route has a policy object: priority metrics (latency, cost, accuracy), SLO targets, and a fallback chain.
- Example policy for chat: {preferred: redwood-chat-lowlat, SLO: p95 < 200ms, fallback: redwood-chat-econ -> redwood-chat-compat}. For batch summarization: {preferred: redwood-summarize-econ, SLO: throughput >= 500 reqs/min, cost cap: $X/token, fallback: redwood-summarize-compat}.
- We can codify this in config (YAML/JSON) and push via the Console API; Dev can set canary rollouts.

3) Structured output / tool calling
- We support both approaches: structured JSON output with strict schema enforcement and an integrated tool-calling shim. For ACME I recommend structured output for ticketing (deterministic fields) and tool calling for search/query flows where you want Redwood to trigger functions (we provide a local shim and SDK helpers).

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- Recommendation: generate embeddings via Redwood for indexing into OpenSearch, but use a lightweight reranker on-hotpath (Redwood reranker or your custom model). For failover, keep your existing pipeline: if Redwood embeddings service is unavailable, your index still works with legacy embeddings.

Next steps (T+):
- Dev: review attached integration note + diagram (ACME_Redwood_MVP_integration_notes.pdf).
- Dev + Redwood infra (Dev Patel): schedule 60m architecture sync to map auth flow and networking (mtls/VPC).
- Redwood: share sample policy configs & SDK snippet.

Can we tentatively schedule the sync for Tuesday 3/23 10am PT?

Thanks,

Elena — looping in a few architecture details ahead of the sync. A few clarifications and config examples below.

Auth & SDK notes:
- Node SDK can accept either a long-lived service token stored in your KMS or we support short-lived tokens via our token service. If you want private deployment, we also support mutual TLS and VPC peering.
- Sample snippet (pseudo):
  const client = new Redwood({apiKey: await kms.getSecret('redwood/service-token')});
  const resp = await client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-chat-lowlat', input});

Routing & policy config (concrete example):
- Route JSON (example, simplified):
  route: acme-chat
  policy:
    metrics: [latency_p95, cost_per_token]
    targets: {latency_p95: 200}
    preferred: ['redwood-chat-lowlat']
    fallback: ['redwood-chat-econ','redwood-chat-compat']
    region_pref: ['us-west-2', 'us-east-1']
- The Console API accepts these route objects; you can version them and assign rollout percentages for canaries.
- Fallback behavior: requests that violate SLO (e.g., latency spike) automatically switch to next candidate in the fallback chain. You can also enforce cost caps per route.

Embeddings/rerankers:
- We recommend batch-indexing embeddings (export via SDK), then run periodic reranking with either Redwood reranker or your service. For on-demand rerank in chat flows, call the embeddings endpoint with a small beam and then call the reranker model; we provide a helper in the SDK to compose these calls.

Operational notes:
- Telemetry: token-level cost and latency breakouts are available per route.
- Canary: start 10% traffic to the new route for 48 hours with rollback on quality/regression alerts.

I’ll attach a sample route config to the Drive link. Looking forward to Tuesday.

Elena — one quick note from pricing/ops side before the architecture sync:

- For the pilot I recommend reserving a small dedicated pool (monthly commit) for chat traffic if you need consistent p95 latency; otherwise hosted with routing to low-lat models + caching works well for cost control.
- Cost/latency trade-off example: redwood-chat-lowlat (higher $/token, p95 ~120ms) vs redwood-chat-econ (lower $/token, p95 ~350ms). You can set a per-route cost cap to prevent surprise spend.
- Also consider KV prefix caching for chat sessions — reduces tokens and improves p95. We can instrument expected token reductions after we see a sample workload.

I’ll bring a short SLO/cost comparison table to the call. If ACME wants we can provision a short-lived demo tenant to exercise routing & fallback policies during the sync.

Thanks,
Marcus
